title: Transit at Dawn
briefing: A cracked junction has closed the city rail interchange just before the morning shift. Replacement buses can cover workers or hospital routes, but not both at full frequency.

private_intelligence.infrastructure: The bypass can carry half the usual trains, but running it continuously postpones the only safe repair window.
private_intelligence.community: Night-shift cleaners and unpaid carers are missing from the essential-worker register; eligibility checks would strand them.
private_intelligence.economy: The freight depot shares bus drivers with public transport; reallocating all drivers will delay food deliveries.
private_intelligence.safety: Hospital shuttle stops have supervised boarding, while the general interchange has no safe queue space.

choices.title: Prioritize Registered Staff
choices.description: Reserve replacement buses for registered essential workers.
choices.consequence: Hospitals regain reliable staffing, but excluded workers lose shifts and faith in the eligibility register.

choices.title: Run Shared Frequent Loops
choices.description: Use open-access loops and close the junction for repairs.
choices.consequence: Open buses distribute access and create a repair window, while slower arrivals cost businesses working hours.

choices.title: Keep the Bypass Running
choices.description: Operate limited rail service and reserve buses for vulnerable riders.
choices.consequence: More workplaces remain reachable, but continuous bypass use adds wear and leaves the cracked junction unrepaired.
